<!-- pr-reviewer: baa356d200ba5f4b2ded7989d5a702c9e402b09d -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge. SAFETY-tier review. No blocking findings.

The constrained mesher uses the requested chord tolerance. The existing planner, continuous-deviation, weld, triangle-budget, topology and volume checks remain active. Cancellation prevents a new fallback and is checked after planning. Mesher errors and panics remain named refusals.

The two regression tests check the STEP and Solidcraft models at 0.005 mm. They check a closed mesh, 13 faces and the analytic volume. The new STEP fixture has its agreement test and inventory row.

## Local build and tests

Reviewed the trial merge `6241854c8cb22c3d2c97b0d159e0a0ba5f92e89a` with upstream main `f14097855b0e347a073f1e8cc74a889554e6dbbb`. Its first parent is the PR head above. Applied the laws from upstream main's AGENTS.md.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 97 steps passed, 0 failed, 12.4 minutes. Builds passed for geometry, kernel, app and UI. The suites passed 2,297 tests; 34 tests were ignored in this debug run.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 261 steps passed, 0 failed, 83.8 minutes. The reached kernel, motion and app lanes ran in release mode. They passed 112 tests. The gate also checked four declared known failures at their expected assertions: three for #1950 and one for #2849.
- UI suites ran from `crates/ui`. No runner or workflow was used.

## Extra suites run

Searched test sources for `testdata/models` readers. Ran every selected fixture-reader suite in the quick gate. The table below names each suite and its result.

The required importer checks also ran explicitly as gate steps:

- `camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement`: 29 passed.
- `camcraft-kernel --test machining_mesh`: 7 passed.
- `camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join`: 5 passed.

## Mutations

Repeated the PR's rollback check separately for both regression pins. Temporarily used upstream main's `machining_mesh.rs` in the throwaway worktree.

1. `hole_on_pocket_wall_meshes_within_tolerance`: red, exit 101. Face 12 was capped at 3.306568238717226 mm sag for 0.005 mm.
2. `hole_on_pocket_wall_solidcraft_meshes_within_tolerance`: red, exit 101. Face 12 was capped at 3.3065682387172393 mm sag for 0.005 mm.

Restored the reviewed source. Both tests then passed. The worktree has no source changes.

## Golden and scope checks

No existing golden changed. Read the new agreement row line by line: it records `off: area` for the raw display planner. It does not change the machining acceptance checks. No `.nc`, `.cl` or UI snapshot changed. The PR changes no UI source, dependency, workflow or process file.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes

The full release gate and manual GUI import were not run. The shared-face finishing heavy suite passed all six bands; it took about 35 minutes. The raw display planner still has the area discrepancy stated in the PR body.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head baa356d200ba5f4b2ded7989d5a702c9e402b09d. This comment has no review marker. I did not change a label.

Verdict: no blocker.

## Safety
- The fallback (`crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:299-308`) gives its result to the same checks as before: `judge()` (:151-180), the triangle budget (:319), the deviation check (:327-345), then weld, watertightness and volume.
- I found no path to a mesh that is silently wrong. Each new failure is a named refusal. A panic in the mesher becomes `Planner("the planner panicked")`.
- The new code adds no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`, and no new float or index math.
- A model that passed before cannot change. The fallback starts only where `judge` refused with `FaceCapped`.

## Notes, not blockers
- The fallback starts for a capped face of each surface type, not only for a cylinder. The title says less than the code. The decision file states the scope correctly.
- The refusal class can change from `FaceCapped` to `Planner(..)` when the fallback fails also. It stays a refusal.
- The mesher takes no cancel token. Cancellation is checked before and after the call, not during it.
- Nothing says that the fallback ran.

## Tests and form
- The two pins assert 0.005 mm, a closed mesh, 13 faces and the analytic volume. The reviewer's mutation run shows them red without the fix.
- The row `off: area` is correct: the bench judges the raw display plan, not the machining mesh.
- Placement, Gate map, provenance, the 400-line limit (395), the decision file and the body are correct.
- The fixture is a small SolidCraft model (25,778 bytes). The algorithm is a call to the public API of solidcore-tess.

## Not checked
I did not build. The trial merge with the current `main` (835556814) is in the queue here. The heavy result in the review used an older `main` (f14097855).

Follow-ups filed: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3511 and https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3512.
